designChangesAfterCp1.why: Measured on this workstation 2026-09-17: `process.exit()` immediately after an undici (fetch) response crashes libuv on Windows with `Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)` and exit 0xC0000409, which destroys the verdict's exit code. That is DEV_PROCESS 2.3's exact failure mode — the proof is on the real exit code, and here the real exit code was the thing being destroyed. The loop now drains and exits cleanly in ~1.4s.

designChangesAfterCp1.change: inventory-key-consumers.mjs: the per-project Vercel reads were restructured to async + bounded concurrency (mapLimit, 4), each call given its own throwaway directory with a hand-written .vercel/project.json.
designChangesAfterCp1.why: The first version spawned a blocking CLI per project and shared one scaffolding directory. Two defects, both found by reading my own code rather than by a failure: the blocking spawn made the declared concurrency a fiction, and shared scaffolding is exactly how the 2026-08-10 trap (`.vercel/project.json` naming the wrong project) gets repeated. Also removed a `STATED_GAPS_OUT` reference left behind by the refactor, which threw at runtime.

designChangesAfterCp1.change: The runbook's pairing table was rewritten AFTER the inventory ran, not from the dispatch's prose.
designChangesAfterCp1.why: The first draft repeated the dispatch's sentence. Reading the inventory JSON at source produced two corrections to it: (a) `property-explorer` production carries a variable literally NAMED `HAUSKA_ENGINE_API_KEY` (last written 2026-07-24, untouched by the rotation) — a third name for the same secret on the same project, and not mentioned in the dispatch; (b) the environment sets are per entry (e.g. `property-explorer-staging` holds CORTEX_SERVICE_API_KEY in production only; `icc-demo` holds RETRIEVAL_API_KEY in production only). The rule 'verify at source, including your own context block' is what produced both.

designChangesAfterCp1.change: The hauska-map PR's first draft contained an inline predicate (grep for `retrieval_auth_failed` / `HTTP 401` plus the 401 status) while its own comment claimed no second implementation existed.
designChangesAfterCp1.why: Self-contradiction, caught in adversarial review of my own diff. A YAML re-implementation of the classifier cannot carry a divergence test against the doc_repo script (DEV_PROCESS 2.4), so the honest move was to delete it rather than to claim parity. The step now prints the fresh preview's URL and the exact command that grades it; the PR writes every environment (the cause) and leaves the predicate single-sourced (the check).

attacked.attack: Does `ok` mean the key is right, or merely that something answered 200?
attacked.outcome: It means the credential leg answered for ONE parcel on ONE URL. It cannot prove every environment of every consumer, and the runbook's Step 3 says so in the same breath as it says what the check can reach. Enumeration is Step 0's job; the two are separate gates on purpose.

attacked.attack: exclusionsWereLoadBearing: is bypass (3) (readPath not asserted) a convenience that hides the failure being hunted?
attacked.outcome: Measured the opposite way round: the dispatch's own falsifier-2 target returns readPath=record today. Asserting readPath would have made this lane's own prescribed falsifier FAIL while the credential leg was demonstrably fine, i.e. folding P-230's finding in would have produced exactly the permanently-red gate DEV_PROCESS 2.0 forbids. The exclusion is load-bearing and is now evidenced rather than asserted.

attacked.attack: Is the self-test vacuous (does it pass because it never fires)?
attacked.outcome: Not vacuous: the recorded 401 body with its auth marker stripped must classify as REFUSAL, and a 200 carrying a marker must classify as auth-failure; both are asserted. The 200 fixture is also checked for NOT carrying a marker, so the PASS case cannot be passing for the wrong reason.

attacked.attack: Can the indicator be observed FIRING live, or only passing live?
attacked.outcome: Refusal fires live (exit 4 on a bogus path). AUTH_FAILURE cannot be made to fire live by this lane at all: it would require an environment whose key is stale, and the dispatch forbids creating one. Residual stated below rather than papered over.

attacked.attack: Does the runbook claim a cadence or a trigger that does not exist?
attacked.outcome: No. It states that neither Step 0 nor Step 3 is scheduled, names why (two authenticated CLIs; a live preview URL), and refuses to claim a cadence — a check that cannot reach its subject is a dead gate.

attacked.attack: Does the hauska-map change, if merged and run, actually close the hole?
attacked.outcome: It closes the WRITE half for project property-explorer only. `hauska-map`'s workflow covers one consumer; the inventory names six Vercel projects holding a copy of one of the aliases or predicate names. The runbook requires the other five to be walked by hand, and says the workflow's scope is one project.

attacked.attack: Would a reader mistake the inventory for a statement that these environments hold the SAME value?
attacked.outcome: The report states in its own header and the runbook repeats it: the predicate is variable NAMES, no value is read, so the listing cannot say two names hold one value. The command-center / cmdcenter / icc-demo copies last written in July and August are reported as 'untouched by the 2026-09-16 rotation', with the observation that whether that is drift or a different value is a decision a rotation must take — not as a finding of drift.

residualWeaknesses: The AUTH_FAILURE branch has never fired against a live host in this lane's run — only against the recorded 401 body. A live stale preview was not created because creating one is forbidden here. The first real firing will be the first real rotation or the first environment that genuinely drifts; until then the auth branch's live evidence is the recorded body plus the classifier's unit cases.

The check measures one URL that a human hands it. Nothing schedules it and nothing enumerates previews for it; a rotation that forgets to run it is still uncaught by machinery. P-279's class of preventive post-deploy checks is the shape that would catch the forgetting, and it is a different row.
The inventory's version of 'every consumer' is bounded by two CLIs' visibility: the six stated gaps are real holes, and any of them could hold a copy.
The hauska-map workflow change is unmerged and unrun. Until it is both, a rotation performed by running that workflow still misses Preview by construction, and only the closing check will say so.
